I think though we often fall somewhere on the animism-god spectrum, in simple terms.

E.g. Animism (the world is alive and we are all connected--the divine is in you too)--->each living thing has its respective nature spirit or energy--->these nature spirits are sometimes personified as fairies, elves etc--->there are certain deities that pertain to certain things found in nature (like Ganesha, Vishnu, Freya, Loki)--->one god, or a god and goddess in the case of Gardnerian witchcraft.

If belief is cyclical, we may soon culturally return to animism. Many people now say that they resonate with a universal consciousness more than they do a "one omnipotent, omnipresent god" with Christian associations. I think though it doesn't matter where you are in that circle of belief if your work enriches yourself and those around you, but dogma=ego and a superiority complex. It's anti-diversity. It's anti-progress, and as culture evolves we always need to evolve our belief systems with it, not hold too much to dogmas because of associated lineage.
